reason: The hypothesis combines three distinct elements—electro spark deposition (ESD) as a low-heat-input repair method, a CrFeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy composite with in-situ carbide formers, and application to hot-cracking-sensitive Cr–Ni–Mo steel—into a single proposal. No single passage combines all three; P1 studies laser repair of 34CrNiMo6, P18 uses ESD for a CrFeCoNi medium-entropy alloy on a different steel, and P2/P3 add WC to HEA coatings via laser cladding. The hypothesis links these through a mechanism (ESD's localized heating prevents hot cracking while rapid solidification and carbide reinforcement enhance properties) that none of the passages states for this material system.
copied_elements: ESD minimizes heat input and prevents hot cracking (P1, P26)
HEA coatings improve hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance (P2, P6, P8, P15)
WC or carbide additives form in-situ hard phases (P2, P3, P16, P38)
Nano-CeO2 refines grain and improves properties (P2, P25, P39)
34CrNiMo6 steel is prone to wear and needs repair (P1, P5, P7)
Laser cladding is a common HEA coating method (P6, P9, P11, P33)
